Hypothesis: The binding mechanism is late-charge: at high SOC the anode potential is lowest and cumulative heating peaks, so maintaining 1.5C through steps 3-4 caused both the 7.304 mV anode minimum and 51.191 degC peak in the baseline. Front-loading current early, when anode potential is higher and the cell is cooler, and tapering late should recover feasibility with less time penalty than a uniform rate cut.

Baseline result res_daf139b4872f25a0d7d53ea2 at uniform 1.5C gave 28.203 min but min_anode_potential 7.304 mV (needs >=10) and max_temperature 51.191 degC (needs <=45). Uniform-rate time for the proposed steps is 60*0.175*(1/1.5+1/1.4+1/1.1+1/0.8) ~= 37.2 min before any CV addition. Mean squared C-rate falls to ~0.67 of baseline, scaling the 26.2 degC rise to roughly 42-43 degC peak, and cutting the final step to 0.8C should raise the late-SOC anode minimum. Ambient 25 degC stays within the stated 23-27 degC validity range.

Hypothesis: Temperature, not anode potential, now binds: in res_0f270c06b1c43eb836e29a8d the peak temperature 44.522 degC (only 0.478 degC below the 45 degC limit) occurs at the end of step 3 at 62.5% SOC, then temperature falls during the 0.8C step 4 to about 41.1 degC, while min_anode_potential is 25.912 mV (15.912 mV above the 10 mV limit) and occurs at 80% SOC. So the final step is thermally slack and anode-slack: raising c_rate_4 should buy time using that late slack, whereas raising c_rate_3 would directly raise the binding step-3 temperature peak.

Previous prediction was inside on all quantities for res_0f270c06b1c43eb836e29a8d (37.17 vs 37.5 min, 44.522 vs 42.5 degC, 25.912 vs 18 mV), so the tapered mechanism held, but temperature came in hotter than predicted and is now the expected binding constraint. Nominal step time is 10.5/C min per 17.5% SOC step: 7.0+7.5+9.545+10.5 = 34.545 min at 1.5/1.4/1.1/1.0C, saving 2.625 min in step 4 alone versus 0.8C. The first three steps are unchanged, so the step-3 temperature peak of 44.522 degC in res_0f270c06b1c43eb836e29a8d should recur; at 1.0C step-4 heating should make temperature fall more slowly rather than exceed that peak. The anode drop for +0.2C late is estimated from the reference-search sensitivity (uniform 1.0C in res_3068a21fb9d4e3b494d4523b to 1.2C in res_3cbc4977d0f635bbdca145d3 lowered min_anode_potential by about 3.1 mV per 0.2C), applied to the 25.912 mV starting margin, giving roughly 20 mV. Ambient 25 degC is within the 23-27 degC validity range; rates are within 0.2-1.5C bounds, though charge above 0.3C remains unvalidated by records as noted in the state.

Hypothesis: Temperature, not anode potential, is now the binding constraint: the incumbent at 1.5/1.4/1.1/1.0 C peaks at 44.522 degC (0.478 degC below the 45 degC limit) while its anode minimum is 16.737 mV (6.737 mV above the 10 mV limit). Raising only step 3, whose end sets up the temperature peak, tests thermal binding; raising step 4 instead would attack the anode minimum directly, since the +0.2 C step-4 increase last turn dropped the anode minimum by 9.175 mV.

Previous prediction for res_4c2e49d3a23bc20e7df45ae5 was inside on all quantities (34.545 vs 34.6 min, 44.522 vs 44.5 degC, 16.737 vs 20.0 mV), but the anode drop from raising c_rate_4 (25.912 mV in res_0f270c06b1c43eb836e29a8d to 16.737 mV) was larger than the reference-search sensitivity suggested, so step 4 is not pushed again. Nominal time at 1.5/1.4/1.2/1.0 C is 10.5*(1/1.5+1/1.4+1/1.2+1/1.0)=33.75 min, saving 0.795 min over the 34.545 min incumbent and remaining faster than the 40.008 min reference in res_fa3ada4202002bb51e53f1b0 if feasible. The temperature series for rq_557dfad98ee08b4d502a rises through step 3 toward the 44.522 degC peak, while the anode minimum occurs at the end of step 4, so a step-3-only increase should mainly move temperature, with the final anode minimum staying near 16.7 mV. Ambient 25 degC is within the 23-27 degC validity range and rates are within 0.2-1.5C bounds; charge above 0.3C remains unvalidated by records, as noted in the state.

Hypothesis: Temperature binds at the end of step 3 and anode potential binds at the end of step 4, on different steps. The step-3 increase in res_14ce301aab1aac4b56762931 raised the peak from 44.522 to 45.58 degC (+1.058 degC for +0.1 C, outside my 44.5-45.4 degC interval), confirming strong step-3 thermal coupling, while its anode minimum stayed slack at 17.742 mV. In the incumbent res_4c2e49d3a23bc20e7df45ae5 temperature already falls throughout the 1.0 C step 4 (44.522 degC peak at end of step 3, falling thereafter), so step 4 is thermally slack but anode-limited: raising only c_rate_4 should buy time until the anode minimum, which fell 9.175 mV when c_rate_4 rose 0.8 to 1.0 C between res_0f270c06b1c43eb836e29a8d and res_4c2e49d3a23bc20e7df45ae5, approaches 10 mV.

Comparison with the last prediction first: for res_14ce301aab1aac4b56762931 charge time (33.75 vs 33.75 min) and anode (17.742 vs 16.0 mV, inside 11-21 mV) were inside, but max_temperature 45.58 degC fell outside the 44.5-45.4 degC interval. I therefore revise the belief: step-3 rate couples to the temperature peak about twice as strongly as estimated (+1.058 degC per +0.1 C observed), so step 3 is not raised again and the expected binding constraint for any step-3 move is temperature. The incumbent rq_557dfad98ee08b4d502a (res_4c2e49d3a23bc20e7df45ae5) at 1.5/1.4/1.1/1.0 C meets every constraint at 34.545 min, with temperature 44.522 degC (0.478 degC margin) peaking at end of step 3 and anode 16.737 mV (6.737 mV margin) at end of step 4. Nominal time at 1.5/1.4/1.1/1.1 C is 10.5*(1/1.5+1/1.4+1/1.1+1/1.1)=33.59 min, saving 0.955 min in step 4 alone. The anode estimate applies the observed step-4 sensitivity from res_0f270c06b1c43eb836e29a8d to res_4c2e49d3a23bc20e7df45ae5 (25.912 to 16.737 mV for +0.2 C, about -4.6 mV per +0.1 C) to the 16.737 mV incumbent value, giving about 12.1 mV; the wide interval reflects that this sensitivity was larger than the reference-search sensitivity suggested earlier. Temperature should stay near the unchanged step-3 peak of 44.522 degC because temperature fell during the whole 1.0 C step 4 in the incumbent series; the hi bound allows for a small new late peak at 1.1 C. Ambient 25 degC is within the 23-27 degC validity range and all rates are within the 0.2-1.5 C bounds; charge above 0.3 C remains unvalidated by records, as noted in the state, so this is a simulation result, not physical proof.

Hypothesis: Temperature, peaking at the end of step 3, is the expected binding constraint, with anode potential at the end of step 4 second. The incumbent 1.5/1.4/1.1/1.0 C (res_4c2e49d3a23bc20e7df45ae5) peaks at 44.522 degC (0.478 degC margin) at end of step 3 and has anode 16.737 mV (6.737 mV margin) at end of step 4. Step 3 is thermally capped (1.1 to 1.2 C raised peak by 1.058 degC to 45.58 degC in res_14ce301aab1aac4b56762931) and step 4 is anode/thermal capped (1.0 to 1.1 C dropped anode 16.737 to 12.309 mV and raised peak 44.522 to 44.951 degC, straddling 45 degC, in res_7babf83ecf7eeff6acf4f646). Step 2 is the only untested lever: raising it to the 1.5 C bound buys nominal time from an earlier step whose heat has step 3 to partly dissipate, so it may cost less peak temperature per minute saved than step 3 did.

Comparison with last prediction first: for res_7babf83ecf7eeff6acf4f646 all quantities were inside (33.593 vs 33.59 min, 44.951 vs 44.6 degC inside 44.5-45.1, 12.309 vs 12.1 mV), but the result is inconclusive because 44.951 ± 0.1 degC straddles the 45 degC limit, and the step-4 increase raised the temperature peak by 0.429 degC rather than leaving it at the step-3 peak — so late/early heating carries into the peak more than the incumbent series suggested. Nominal time at 1.5/1.5/1.1/1.0 C is 10.5*(1/1.5+1/1.5+1/1.1+1/1.0)=34.045 min, saving 0.5 min in step 2 alone versus the 34.545 min incumbent rq_557dfad98ee08b4d502a, which already meets every constraint and is faster than the 40.008 min reference in res_fa3ada4202002bb51e53f1b0. The anode minimum occurs at end of step 4 at unchanged 1.0 C, so it should stay near the incumbent 16.737 mV, discounted for extra polarisation from a faster step 2. Temperature is predicted just below the limit with a hi bound above it, reflecting the strong thermal coupling seen for step 3 (+1.058 degC per +0.1 C) and step 4 (+0.429 degC per +0.1 C). Ambient 25 degC is within the 23-27 degC validity range and all rates are within 0.2-1.5 C bounds; charge above 0.3C remains unvalidated by records, so this is a simulation result, not physical proof.

Hypothesis: Under objective v2 the anode constraint now binds first: re-checking earlier results, the incumbent 1.5/1.4/1.1/0.8C (res_0f270c06b1c43eb836e29a8d) passes at 25.912 mV, only 0.912 mV above the new 25 mV limit, with temperature 44.522 degC, 0.478 degC below its limit, whereas every faster v1 candidate fails v2 on anode (16.737 mV in res_4c2e49d3a23bc20e7df45ae5, 17.742 mV and 45.58 degC in res_14ce301aab1aac4b56762931). Because the anode minimum occurs at the end of step 4 at unchanged 0.8C, raising only step 2 to its 1.5C bound should buy time mainly at a temperature cost, with little direct anode cost.

Comparison with the incumbent first: rq_f56e82af08890ee5eaf4 at 1.5/1.4/1.1/0.8C gave 37.17 min, 44.522 degC and 25.912 mV, inside its wide prediction interval, and under v2 it is the only candidate that meets the constraints; I therefore revise the prior belief that temperature alone binds — at v2 both constraints are tight, anode marginally tighter in normalised terms. Nominal time at 1.5/1.5/1.1/0.8C is 10.5*(1/1.5+1/1.5+1/1.1+1/0.8)=36.67 min, saving 0.50 min in step 2 alone. Step 3 is not raised because +0.1C there raised the peak by 1.058 degC to 45.58 degC in res_14ce301aab1aac4b56762931, and step 4 is not raised because +0.2C there dropped the anode minimum by 9.175 mV between res_0f270c06b1c43eb836e29a8d and res_4c2e49d3a23bc20e7df45ae5, which would breach the 25 mV limit. The step-2 heat has the whole of step 3 to partly dissipate before the end-of-step-3 temperature peak, so its temperature cost per minute saved should be lower than step 3's; the wide anode interval reflects untested early-to-late coupling. Ambient 25 degC is within the 23-27 degC validity range and all rates are within 0.2-1.5C bounds; charge above 0.3C remains unvalidated by records (see res_e690e2371b73ae45184a5f31 validity notes), so this is a simulation result, not physical proof, and the reference search for v2 has not finished, so speed versus the reference is not yet compared.

conclusion.text: In simulation, the tapered protocol 1.5C, 1.4C, 1.1C, 0.8C reaches 80 % SOC in 37.2 min with the anode at +25.9 mV and the cell at 44.5 C, meeting the amended +25 mV margin and the 45 C limit. The fastest single-step constant-current charge the reference search found under the same limits takes 70 min (0.6C). The planner stopped on its model budget after five experiments.
